paper: How much evidence can a simulator leave?
subtitle: Explicit evidence rates, a one-draw cap, and what the NIST beacon and Delft 2015 data do and do not show
author: simulation-theory contributors

claims.name: unrestricted indistinguishability
claims.status: elementary, not claimed as new
assumptions: the simulator class contains a member whose induced law on the full observable space equals the base law
nonclaims: does not make restricted simulator hypotheses untestable
not evidence for or against the hypothesis that reality is simulated

claims.name: pathwise sandwich
claims.status: upper regret bound classical (Krichevsky-Trofimov; Willems-Shtarkov-Tjalkens); uniform lower bound stated with an explicit constant, no priority claimed (cf. Freund 1996; Xie-Barron 2000)
assumptions: binary sequences of any length n >= 1
Krichevsky-Trofimov (Jeffreys) mixture against fair bits
nonclaims: no priority is claimed for two-sided pathwise KT or Jeffreys regret bounds
holds for every sequence, so it is not a property of any particular data source

claims.name: non-asymptotic expected sandwich
claims.status: expected upper bound new; lower half is ST-T271 (standard)
assumptions: bits IID Bernoulli(q) under the alternative, q in [0, 1]
Jeffreys prior on q; fair-bit base law
every n >= 1
nonclaims: the 1.47-nat window is explicit, not sharp
does not cover dependent, adaptive or adversarial sources

claims.name: the constant
claims.status: Clarke-Barron expansion specialized; re-derived, not new
assumptions: fixed q; interior and boundary q treated separately
nonclaims: the o(1) term is pointwise in q, not uniform near q in {0, 1}

claims.name: remainder table
claims.status: bounded
assumptions: 60-digit arithmetic on the declared grid q in {1/10, 1/5, 1/4, 1/3, 2/5, 1/2} at n = 5000, plus beacon scale q = 1/2, n = 131072
nonclaims: a bounded table, not a proof of the second-order remainder (open problem ST-O02)

claims.name: second-order KT remainder
claims.status: heuristically derived; remainder control not written
assumptions: interior q
nonclaims: the conjectured (1 - 2q)^2 / (24 n q (1 - q)) term is not proved; numerical agreement is not a proof

claims.name: pathwise rejection region and power frontier
claims.status: elementary; uses binary Pinsker and Hoeffding
assumptions: IID bits
alpha, beta in (0, 1)
level alpha under optional stopping by Ville's inequality
nonclaims: the sufficient frontier and the converse ST-T276 differ by a factor of order sqrt(ln n); they do not match

claims.name: converse
claims.status: Le Cam two-point method with Pinsker and Bretagnolle-Huber; not new
assumptions: randomized tests on n IID bits, including sequential tests stopped by time n
nonclaims: no matching constant with the sufficient frontier is claimed

claims.name: coarsened observation
claims.status: exact inside the declared channel model; extends ST-M83
assumptions: every bit passes independently through a known binary symmetric channel with flip probability kappa in [0, 1/2)
nonclaims: unknown or dependent coarsening channels are not covered

claims.name: one-draw cap
claims.status: data-processing inequality, applied to world-level weights; standard
assumptions: both hypotheses share the transcript kernel K
experimenter policy does not depend on the hypothesis label
the N-unit form assumes independent world draws
nonclaims: vacuous when a is not absolutely continuous with respect to b
bounds expected evidence about world-level weights only; does not limit learning which world is active

claims.name: saturation identity
claims.status: standard: KL chain rule; zero-gap condition specializes the Kullback-Leibler sufficiency condition; only the finite-M ratio form and the counterexamples are offered
assumptions: KL(a || b) finite
finite M with component densities w.r.t. a common dominating measure for the zero-gap condition
nonclaims: the converse of 'M a function of Y implies zero gap' fails in general

claims.name: gap bound and decay
claims.status: (R - 1) factor and support-mismatch term new; MAP-error Chernoff exponent classical
assumptions: finite M with a absolutely continuous with respect to b
conditionally IID transcripts for the decay statement
every relevant component pair has distinct one-step laws
nonclaims: the gap decays at least as fast as the stated exponent; the exponent is not shown to be tight

claims.name: different kernels
claims.status: chain rule plus data processing; standard
assumptions: the hypotheses may use different kernels K^a and K^b
nonclaims: no matching lower bound is claimed

claims.name: persistent audit
claims.status: bounded exact-law audit
assumptions: exact rational laws over sufficient count vectors with 60-digit logarithms, declared examples up to T = 64
nonclaims: bounded instances corroborate the proofs; they are not proofs

claims.name: betting e-processes
claims.status: conditional-null extension of ST-T08; Bell-test supermartingales and beta-mixture closed forms are standard; only the exact rational closed form is new
assumptions: the win-rate null holds conditionally on the full past
mixing law fixed independently of the data, or predictable bets
trial order is the physical time order
nonclaims: does not say which resource level is physically correct

claims.name: growth ceiling and sample-size floor
claims.status: Kelly and Wald bounds; standard
assumptions: IID Bernoulli truth for the ceiling
for the floor: almost surely finite stopping time with finite mean under the truth
nonclaims: not a new inequality

claims.name: uniform-setting statistical strength
claims.status: the v = 1 value reproduces van Dam, Gill and Grunwald; only the v-family and the data-processing proof are new
assumptions: uniform settings independent of the hidden variable
isotropic CHSH law with visibility v in [0, 1]
nonclaims: the v = 1 value is not new

claims.name: beacon evidence
claims.status: bounded; not a randomness certification
assumptions: pinned NIST beacon pulse list, 131072 bits
composite KT test against fair bits at alpha = 0.01
nonclaims: not a randomness certification; NIST signatures are not checked
the pathwise sandwich holds for every sequence, so its agreement is a check of the computation, not of the source

claims.name: beacon power frontier
claims.status: bounded; exact 60-digit powers on a declared grid
assumptions: IID biased sources only
nonclaims: says nothing about non-IID deviations from fair bits

claims.name: Delft recomputation and disk placement
claims.status: bounded; reproduces the published statistic
assumptions: the committed Delft 2015 valid trials (n = 245) and the published setting-predictability model
nonclaims: the fixed-n p = 0.039 assumes n fixed independently of the data
not evidence for or against the hypothesis that reality is simulated

claims.name: escape-route frontiers
claims.status: frontier (b) reproduces Pironio; (d) is the Putz et al. bound; (a) possibly known; new: exact dual certificates and attaining models
assumptions: parts (a) to (c): uniform settings independent of the shared randomness and of the past
part (d): local outputs, setting law may depend on the hidden variable with p(x, y | lambda) >= l; S bound under uniform observed settings
per-trial budgets
nonclaims: budgets that hold only on average over a run are not covered
(b) and (d) are not new

claims.name: Delft anytime check
claims.status: bounded; negative result; covers constant-bet mixtures on the win indicator only
assumptions: constant-bet mixtures on the CHSH win indicator fixed independently of the data
per-trial budgets holding conditionally on the past
the published setting-predictability model and RNG independence
nonclaims: does not cover full-data test factors, adaptive bets, or e-processes valid only for narrower model classes
does not show that no anytime-valid test could reject on these data

context_note: cited in prose, in the claims table or in the reproduction map; stated in the repository, not restated as a result box here
paper_nonclaims: nothing in the paper is evidence for or against simulation
proofs are written in the repository derivation documents and are not formally verified
the renderer results summarized in Section 7 are stated in the companion manuscript and the repository, not proved here
